tolerances.//: How far a re-derived number may sit from the one recorded here.
tolerances.//1: The plant is deterministic — two runs of the same binary produce
tolerances.//2: byte-identical stats CSVs — so a disagreement is a real movement,
tolerances.//3: not noise, and these could in principle be a millisecond.  They are
tolerances.//4: not, because a Chrono or compiler change may legitimately move the
tolerances.//5: last digit.  What they must be is far tighter than the slack the
tolerances.//6: [Runway] cases run on: the tightest settle is 2.96 s against a 2.0 s
tolerances.//7: requirement, so 0.96 s of drift would eat the settle while every
tolerances.//8: assertion stayed green.  0.05 s catches that 19x over.
tolerances.//9: release_s is read from the scenario log (millisecond resolution);
tolerances.//10: crossing_s is read from the stats CSV, whose sample period is 0.02 s
tolerances.//11: for all seven, so its floor is a couple of samples rather than a ms.
